control_flow: driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT is below 30 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is in front, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left (10/40); else curve right (40/10).

likely_intent.description: Get the robot through the tunnel and out the other side.

decision_points.condition: the light from above (LLIGHT) is below 30 %

branches.reason: In the simulator the light inside a tunnel only drops to 40 %, so it is never below 30 %.
branches.outcome: light below 30 %: it drives forward at 30 % in the dark
light 30 % or more (bright or dim in a tunnel): it goes on to stopAtWall

decision_points.condition: an obstacle is right in front (FRONT)

branches.outcome: an obstacle is in front: it stops
nothing in front: it goes on to followLine

scenarios.coded_response: Because the light is never below 30 %, it never drives forward in the dark: it finds nothing in front and follows the line. If the line runs on through the tunnel it follows it out; if the line ends in the dark it curves right and circles in place.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is on a line that runs from bright light into a tunnel; inside the tunnel the light is dim (about 40 %) but never below 30 %.
scenarios.trigger: The robot reaches and enters the tunnel.
scenarios.title: Gets through the tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say whether a line runs through the tunnel; the program needs one both to reach the tunnel and to cross it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It gets through the tunnel and comes out the other side.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops while the wall is in front.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is on a line in bright light, and a wall is right in front of it.
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at something in front
